rules.title: Missing out-punch
rules.text: Time & Attendance Policy §2.1: Every shift must end with an OUT punch. If an OUT punch is missing, a manager may add one only at a time supported by evidence (scheduled end or last recorded activity) and never later than 2 hours after the scheduled end.

rules.title: Missing in-punch
rules.text: Time & Attendance Policy §2.2: Every shift must begin with an IN punch. A missing IN punch may be added by a manager at a time supported by evidence, no earlier than 2 hours before the scheduled start and before the recorded OUT punch.

rules.title: Duplicate punch
rules.text: Time & Attendance Policy §2.3: Two punches of the same type within 10 minutes are treated as a device duplicate. The later punch is voided and the earlier one stands.

rules.title: Missing break-end punch
rules.text: Time & Attendance Policy §2.4: A break that was started must be ended. A missing BREAK_END may be added only between the break start and the next recorded punch, and the break may not be recorded as longer than 2 hours.

rules.title: Unparseable punch sequence
rules.text: Time & Attendance Policy §2.9: Punch sequences that cannot be interpreted (for example punches after an OUT, or a BREAK_END with no BREAK_START) must be reviewed manually. No automatic correction is allowed.

rules.title: Implausible shift length
rules.text: Time & Attendance Policy §3.1: A single shift longer than 16 hours is presumed to contain a punch error. The OUT punch may be corrected to a time supported by evidence, no later than 2 hours after the scheduled end.

rules.title: Meal break missing
rules.text: Time & Attendance Policy §4.1: Employees working more than 5 hours must record an unpaid meal break of at least 30 minutes. A missing break is never added retroactively; it is reviewed for meal-premium pay.

rules.title: Meal break too short
rules.text: Time & Attendance Policy §4.2: A recorded meal break shorter than 30 minutes on a shift longer than 5 hours is a violation. Break times are never edited to remove the violation; it is reviewed for meal-premium pay.

rules.title: Weekly overtime exceeded
rules.text: Time & Attendance Policy §5.1: Worked time above 40 hours in the Monday-Sunday pay week is overtime and requires manager approval. Hours are never reduced to avoid overtime.

rules.title: Weekly overtime risk
rules.text: Time & Attendance Policy §5.2: When completed hours plus remaining scheduled hours would exceed 40 for the week, the manager should shorten remaining shifts to stay within 40 hours, or pre-approve the overtime. No shift may be shortened below 4 worked hours.

rules.title: Daily overtime
rules.text: Time & Attendance Policy §5.3: In jurisdictions with daily overtime (US-CA), worked time above 8 hours in one day is overtime and requires manager approval.

rules.title: Schedule deviation
rules.text: Time & Attendance Policy §6.1: Start or end times that differ from the schedule by more than 30 minutes require manager acknowledgement.

rules.title: Unscheduled work
rules.text: Time & Attendance Policy §6.2: Work recorded on a day with no scheduled shift requires manager approval before it is paid.

rules.title: Insufficient rest between shifts
rules.text: Time & Attendance Policy §7.1: Employees must have at least 10 hours between the end of one shift and the start of the next. Shorter gaps are reviewed for rest-period premium pay.

rules.title: Too many consecutive days
rules.text: Time & Attendance Policy §8.1: Employees may not work more than 6 consecutive days. The 7th consecutive day requires manager review.
